overall: Atlanta is running very warm for mid-June, with the current temperature sitting right at the running max of 89.6°F as of 5:34 PM ET. Despite a multi-hour plateau at 89.6°F since 12:50 PM, a still-positive velocity of +1.8°F/hr and a punishing dewpoint of 73.4°F suggest residual heating potential remains. The day has largely met or slightly underperformed the GFS/HRRR consensus, though the NBM (87.5°F) is already clearly busted.
forecast_obs_notes: GFS, ECMWF, and HRRR are tightly clustered at 89.9–90.3°F and remain credible given the 89.6°F observed max; NBM at 87.5°F has already been invalidated. The odd ensemble model (87–88°F, Tier 4) is also busted, while the even model (90–91°F, Tier 1, 58%) aligns well with the NWP suite and current observations.
max_temp_prediction: With the current temp equaling the running max at 89.6°F, a still-positive velocity, and GFS/HRRR pointing to ~89.9°F while ECMWF and the high-confidence even ensemble target 90–90.3°F, a modest final push to just at or just above 90°F is the most likely outcome before cooling accelerates post-sunset. Confidence is moderate-high: the window is narrowing at this hour but the thermal momentum and model consensus support one more tick upward. Best estimate is 90.0°F.
